summary: The Epstein Wall Street Records Act of 2026 requires federal financial regulatory agencies to produce and publicly disclose supervisory records related to Jeffrey Epstein, Ghislaine Maxwell, and their associates. It also mandates investigations into covered financial institutions and their senior executives, requires specific penalties and industry bars for executive misconduct, and directs criminal referrals when violations of federal criminal law are found.

affected_groups.effect: Must collect, submit to Congress, publish online with redactions, investigate, and report on all supervisory records related to Jeffrey Epstein and associated individuals.
Subject to mandatory federal investigations regarding their business relationships, controls, potential document destruction, and potential industry prohibitions or civil penalties.
affected_groups.group: Covered Financial Institutions and Senior Executives

affected_groups.effect: Protected through the mandatory withholding or redaction of their personally identifiable information and personal or medical files from publicly released records.
affected_groups.group: Victims of Jeffrey Epstein and Associates

key_provisions: Requires financial regulatory agencies to submit physical copies of all covered supervisory records to specific congressional committees within 90 days of enactment.

Mandates that agencies make all covered records publicly available in a searchable and downloadable format within 120 days, while redacting victims' personally identifiable information and personal or medical files.

Requires financial regulatory agencies to immediately start investigations into covered financial institutions and senior executives to determine violations of banking, securities, or anti-money laundering laws.

Obligates banking regulators (Federal Reserve, FDIC, OCC) and the SEC to impose industry bans and civil penalties on senior executives who violated laws or aided violations regarding Epstein's financial accounts.
Directs agencies to refer matters to the Attorney General if they reasonably find that a violation of Federal criminal law may have occurred.
Requires the heads of the financial regulatory agencies to submit a detailed report on findings, investigation outcomes, and criminal referrals to specific congressional committees within 180 days.
